analyst.summary: Share India Securities runs a mix of broking, algorithmic trading, margin funding and portfolio management businesses, all of which are closely tied to stock-market trading activity and volatility - which makes its earnings genuinely lumpy quarter to quarter, as shown by profit falling more than a third sequentially even as year-on-year comparisons looked very strong. Indian regulators have also been steadily tightening rules around derivatives trading, a live structural risk for algo/trading-volume-dependent revenue. The stock's cheap valuation (under 12 times earnings) looks like a fair reflection of this volatility and regulatory overhang rather than a bargain being missed.
